statement_review.assessment: Both orientations use actual accepted three filters, preserve input ordering and duplicates, and allow arbitrary linear-order payloads. Empty partitions are harmless algebraic cases; algorithmic nontermination conclusions separately require nonempty or valid rank.

Actual accepted dispatcher calls precisely the same rank and same list. Below works for every natural rank; above exposes k<length because invalid ranks can choose the empty right block. These equalities hold for arbitrary continuation, establishing the recursive branch structurally, not merely that one output happens to be none.

For any fixed deterministic choose operation having the indicated outside value at the specified state, actual runWith consumes one fuel and returns to identical state. Induction covers every finite fuel. The choose-some premise excludes an initial chooser failure; no valid answer or termination is assumed.
A bad choice at just one nonempty list contradicts the existing global membership interface. It does not postulate a global minimum/maximum on arbitrary payload types.

The public one-based boundary is preserved using k+1. Valid sorted-index specifications have a value by length/permutation, so universally exhausted fuel is proved unequal to that specification. Nontermination is the infinite self-recursive path/fuel property, not interpreting any isolated none as divergence.

All sixteen cases connect the new public partition/dispatch/fuel/interface theorems to independent expectations. They include repeated Nat values, negative duplicate Int values, both endpoint ranks, arbitrary fuel and continuation, singleton and empty boundaries, a local policy witness, one-based requests, an invalid above-rank countercase and a successful existing head-pivot contrast.

independent_expected_cases: Below0 on repeated [1,3,1] preserves every zero-based rank and input; above4 preserves valid ranks0..2.
For every finite fuel, below0 and above4 cannot answer valid rank0 or2 on [1,3,1].
Above0 on negative duplicate integers [-3,-1,-3] behaves the same.
Below0 on singleton[1] is a self-recursive state, contrasting with empty-input failure.
A chosen outside pivot at one nonempty input refutes PivotValid; do not assume global below/above operation exists on every ordered type.
Public positive one-based requests fail under those bad policies.
Above-range preservation requires valid rank: rank3 on length3 instead recurses on empty right input with rank0.
Existing in-range head-pivot selection returns the correct largest value on repeated input.
